# openmetadata_database_schema (Resource)

Manages an OpenMetadata database schema. A schema belongs to a database and groups the tables and stored procedures inside it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "openmetadata_database_service" "local_postgres" {
  name         = "local_postgres"
  service_type = "Postgres"
  description  = "Postgres instance used by the analytics team."
}

resource "openmetadata_database" "sales" {
  name    = "sales"
  service = openmetadata_database_service.local_postgres.name
}

resource "openmetadata_database_schema" "public" {
  name         = "public"
  database     = openmetadata_database.sales.fully_qualified_name
  display_name = "Public"
  description  = "Default schema for the sales database."
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `database` (String) Fully qualified name of the database that owns the schema. Changing it replaces the schema.
- `name` (String) Schema name. Changing it replaces the schema, because the name is part of its fully qualified name.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Markdown description of the schema.
- `display_name` (String) Human-readable name shown in the OpenMetadata UI.

### Read-Only

- `fully_qualified_name` (String) Fully qualified name, in the form database.name.
- `id` (String) Server-assigned UUID.
- `updated_at` (String) Last update time in RFC 3339 format.
- `updated_by` (String) User that performed the last update.
- `version` (Number) Server-side entity version.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by UUID.
terraform import openmetadata_database_schema.public 1f6a3a52-8d34-4f4b-9d0f-2f1c1c1c1c1c

# Or import by fully qualified name, in the form database.schema.
terraform import openmetadata_database_schema.public local_postgres.sales.public
```
